elements.element: Audit frequency limited to no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: "no more than once per Calendar Year"; §7.4 "no more than once each Calendar Year"

elements.element: At least 30 days' prior written notice
elements.evidence: "upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice"

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor
elements.evidence: 4.9(a) still permits "Array, and/or an authorized representative reasonably acceptable to Ono" to enter facilities — Array itself, not an independent auditor

No confidentiality undertaking added in 4.9(a); the only such obligation is §7.4's "The Auditor shall be obligated to execute a reasonable confidentiality agreement", which applies to the records audit only

elements.element: Cost shifts to Customer only where underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: §7.4 "underpayment in amounts payable exceeding [ * ] of the amount paid" — threshold redacted; no threshold at all in 4.9(a)

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: "right to examine any internal procedures or records of Ono and/or its Affiliates" and Ono must give "all necessary and reasonable assistance"; no systems-access carve-out inserted

elements.element: Audit no more than once per year
elements.evidence: "no more than once per Calendar Year"
"at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice" exceeds 15 days

elements.element: Cost shifts only where underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: §7.4 threshold is redacted: "exceeding [ * ] of the amount paid"

offending_extra_words: (other than a follow-up inspection reasonably required to verify remediation of a non-compliance previously identified)
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the edit only addresses frequency, notice and cost. It leaves Array (rather than an independent auditor) able to inspect our facilities, adds no confidentiality obligation for the inspecting representative in 4.9(a), and adds no 'no direct access to Customer systems' limit — three preferred elements remain unmet.

The cost-shifting trigger is not tied to a 5% (preferred) or 10% (fallback) underpayment threshold in the redline; the only threshold in the document (§7.4) is redacted, so neither level can be confirmed on cost allocation.

Minimality fails: the inserted parenthetical follow-up-inspection carve-out is a broad new exception that materially undercuts the once-per-year cap we just secured, and it is not needed to complete the preferred level. The official gates also flag the operation as an 11-to-41-word expansion (ratio 3.73) with a 0.745 changed-character ratio.
Intent is preserved: 'Calendar Year' is a defined term, the remaining sentences of 4.9(a) and all of §7.4 continue to operate, and no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.

Suggested tightening: replace only the phrase 'and upon reasonable advance notice' with 'no more than once per Calendar Year, upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice and at Array's expense', drop the follow-up carve-out, and add a short insertion requiring an independent auditor bound by confidentiality and no direct access to Ono's systems.
